reconcile.connective: Commentators read the two commands as targeting different senses of 'child': the humble, trusting temperament to imitate, not the ignorance or fickleness to outgrow.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells's Skeptic's Annotated Bible catalogues this same word-family pairing as contradictory: becoming like a child versus putting away childish things.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.attribution: Steve Wells, Skeptic's Annotated Bible (1999), contra/childish.html

excerpts.excerpt_text: Converting grace makes us like little children, not foolish as children (Co1 14:20), nor fickle (Eph 4:14), nor playful (Mat 11:16) …
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Henry names both Pauline texts (1 Cor 14:20, Eph 4:14) inside his gloss on 'become as little children,' explicitly sorting which childlike traits Christ commends from the childish ones Paul condemns — the row's exact tension, resolved by distinguishing senses of 'child.'
JFB's gloss on 'men' in 1 Cor 14:20 supplies the precise childlike/childish distinction the contradiction turns on, in four words, from the Pauline side of the tension.

pd_work.resource: Matthew Henry, Commentary on the Whole Bible (1706-1714)
pd_work.author: Matthew Henry
pd_work.note: Henry's note on Matthew 18:1-3 treats this exact pairing directly, naming 1 Corinthians 14:20 and Ephesians 4:14 by chapter and verse inside his exposition of 'become as little children' and distinguishing the childlike traits to be imitated from the childish ones Paul warns against.
